transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Zhang (Redwood SE), Sofia Morales (Arbor Head of Data), Ethan Reed (CTO), Priya Nair (Platform Eng)
---
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:00:08] Sofia: Hi Maya, Sofia here, Head of Data at Arbor. We have Ethan and Priya with me.
[00:00:12] Ethan: Hey all.
[00:00:15] Maya: Great. Liam from our SE team will run the console walkthrough - showing usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdowns that folks asked about. We have ~40 minutes, we'll leave time for questions.
[00:00:30] Liam: Thanks. I'll share my screen now - tell me if the slides show up. (brief pause) Can everyone see the Redwood Console?
[00:00:40] Priya: Yes, I can see it. The per-route list is nice.
[00:00:45] Liam: Cool. Top-left is overall usage: requests, tokens in/out, and cost estimate for the period. You can zoom in on a time window and the charts update.
[00:01:05] Liam: Now I'm clicking into a single route - "customer-support:reply" - you can see requests per minute, median latency, p95/p99, and token distribution per response. On the right we show cost per route, broken into model cost, infra premium (if dedicated), and caching savings.
[00:01:25] Sofia: Quick q: how do you attribute cost when a route uses multiple models via fallback?
[00:01:30] Liam: Good question. We attribute by actual model instance used per request and show a stacked breakdown. If a fallback happens 10% of the time to a cheaper model, you'll see that in the % split and the per-route cost line reflects the blended cost.
[00:01:50] Ethan: And can we group by user segment or product line? I.e., show all routes belonging to a product team?
[00:01:57] Liam: Yep, there's tagging - routes can be tagged and you can filter by tag. We demo a group filter now: grouping by "payments" tag consolidates all payment-related routes and shows aggregate cost and latency.
[00:02:15] [00:02:20] Liam: Note on token cost math: we surface tokens consumed, model unit price (per 1k tokens), and derived cost. There's also a column for "effective cost per user request" which divides by successful responses.
[00:02:40] Priya: How accurate is the cost estimate vs invoice? We run high volume, small deltas matter.
[00:02:47] Liam: The console uses the same pricing engine as billing; for hosted accounts it's near-identical. For dedicated, the console shows committed vs uncommitted usage and how burst usage gets billed. Expect rounding differences below 0.5% typically.
[00:03:05] Liam: Now the latency heatmap - you can see percentiles across routes. We automatically flag routes exceeding your SLO (we set a default at p95 > 400ms).
[00:03:20] Sofia: That flagging would help triage. Do you surface root-cause hints?
[00:03:25] Liam: We attach recent traces and the correlated model variant - e.g., whether it's hitting a quantized variant or a fallback model. Also shows whether KV cache hit rate was low which often explains spikes.
[00:03:45] Ethan: Speaking of KV cache - is that inside our VPC in the Private deployment? We need to know data residency.
[00:03:52] Maya: For Private/VPC deployments, caching and KV store can be customer-hosted; for hosted we manage cache with encryption-in-transit and at-rest. We can discuss on security call but summary is you can keep data path inside your network in Private.
[00:04:12] Liam: Back to costs - here's an example per-route breakdown: route A consumed 1.2M tokens, model unit price $0.003/1k tokens, infra add-on $0.0005/1k, caching saved ~18% of tokens. The console projects monthly spend at current rate and shows what switching to a quantized variant or enabling more aggressive prefix caching would save.
[00:04:45] Priya: Can we run hypothetical scenarios? Like if we batch to 16 vs 8, what's the latency/cost tradeoff?
[00:04:52] Liam: Yes - there's a "what-if" simulation panel. You can toggle batch size, model variant, and cache policy; it recomputes projected cost and expected p95. It uses historical latencies and batch scalability curves per model.
[00:05:10] Sofia: How do you handle attribution for multi-tenant calls? Our platform has internal/external tenants.
[00:05:16] Liam: We support tenant id ingestion and you can slice by tenant in the dashboards. If you're sending tenant header we can parse and group automatically.
[00:05:30] [00:05:35] Ethan: Security questions: SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS - what's included?
[00:05:40] Maya: We're SOC2 Type II, support SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning. Audit logs are available in Console and you can stream them to your SIEM. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. We'll send the security pack after this call.
[00:05:58] Priya: Good. Any compliance docs for financial services?
[00:06:03] Maya: Yes, we'll include industry-specific notes and our data residency options.
[00:06:10] Liam: Moving on: per-route anomaly detection. We show a timeline of cost and latency anomalies and list correlated changes - e.g., sudden increase in token length, a model rollout, or a spike in fallback rate. You can drill into the raw requests for a sample window.
[00:06:35] Sofia: That drill-in is useful. Can we export the sample requests? We must scrub PII.
[00:06:40] Liam: Exports are available; we support anonymization rules and retention policies. You can set redaction rules in the Console.
[00:06:55] [00:07:00] Liam: Now demoing per-route cost leaderboard - ranks routes by monthly cost, cost per request, and cost per successful response. The idea is to find the 20% of routes driving 80% of spend.
[00:07:20] Priya: Are system metrics (GPU utilization) tied to routes? If a route is heavy we want to see GPU saturation.
[00:07:27] Liam: We correlate infra metrics to routes by time window. For Dedicated you'll see pool-level GPU usage and which models are occupying GPU slots. That helps justify commit sizes.
[00:07:45] Ethan: If we commit to Dedicated, how do rollouts work? We need canary and automatic fallback to hosted for bursts.
[00:07:52] Maya: Yes - rollouts can be pinned to Dedicated pools and you can configure A/B or canary. For overflow we offer automatic routing to hosted compatible variants with rate limits so you don't hit cold errors.
[00:08:12] Liam: Example: if Dedicated reaches 90% utilization, new requests are routed to a cheaper variant in hosted or queued per policy you choose.
[00:08:25] [00:08:30] Sofia: Pricing: show us a quick comparison - hosted vs dedicated for our traffic shape.
[00:08:35] Liam: I'll pull a sample. (shares spreadsheet) At your projected 50M tokens/month - Hosted estimated $X, Dedicated commit recommended Y GPUs (NVIDIA X) with effective per-token cost reduced ~30% after commit and batching/caching. We'll send exact numbers.
[00:09:05] Priya: We need to see the math for the burst policy - how often will we go to hosted and how is that billed?
[00:09:12] Maya: Burst is billed at the published hosted overage rate; the console will show breakout of committed vs burst usage. We can show historical burst frequency in the cost model we send.
[00:09:28] [00:09:35] Ethan: Integration: are there APIs to pull the per-route metrics into our internal dashboards?
[00:09:40] Liam: Yes, there's a usage metrics API that mirrors Console queries; we also support webhook alerts for anomalies.
[00:09:50] Sofia: Do you support custom SLO alerts and linking to pager duty?
[00:09:54] Liam: Yes, custom SLOs, alerting rules, and PagerDuty/SMS/webhook integrations.
[00:10:05] [00:10:10] Priya: A couple practical things - log retention and export retention limits for trial vs enterprise?
[00:10:15] Maya: Default retention is 30 days for hosted trial; enterprise plans support custom retention up to 365 days or more with add-on. We'll capture your retention needs in the pilot scoping.
[00:10:30] Liam: Quick note on accuracy: sometimes transcription or attribution mis-labels requests if headers missing - console warns when attribution confidence is low.
[00:10:45] [00:10:50] Sofia: Any customers in finance using the per-route cost tool?
[00:10:55] Maya: Yes - several fintechs use it to rework prompts and move low-value routes to smaller models saving 20-40% on spend. We'll share anonymized case studies.
[00:11:10] Liam: We're about half-way; any deep-dive requests?
[00:11:15] Priya: Could you run the what-if on batch size for our typical route? We have quick sample data but will send full traffic.
[00:11:22] Liam: I'll run a quick on-screen simulation using a synthetic route: current batch 8 -> p95 320ms cost $0.0009/request; batch 16 -> p95 410ms cost $0.0006/request. So batching saves cost at some latency increase. You can set SLO constraints to exclude options that exceed your p95 target.
[00:11:48] Ethan: Good. For the pilot, we'd want a 2-week run with a small set of routes, measure cost delta and latency impact. Can you scope that?
[00:11:55] Maya: Yes - pilot scope: 4 routes, 2-week, use our hosted environment first or Private depending on security review. We'll draft a statement of work.
[00:12:10] [00:12:15] Sofia: Timeline: security review may take 2 weeks. We want to start a pilot ASAP.
[00:12:20] Maya: We'll prioritize the security pack in the next 48 hours. Liam will prepare the console deck and short clip.
[00:12:30] Liam: I'll also include steps to instrument tenant headers and route tagging so Priya's team can send sample traffic quickly.
[00:12:40] [00:12:45] Priya: One more Q - can we set cost-based alerts (e.g., if a route exceeds $500/day)?
[00:12:50] Liam: Yes - cost alerts and budget thresholds exist and you can tie them to Slack or PagerDuty.
[00:13:00] Sofia: Ok this has been helpful. Anything else?
[00:13:05] Maya: Quick recap: we'll send pricing & commit math, security docs, console deck + demo clip, and Liam will run a projection with your 7-day sample once you send it. Pilot kickoff week of 3/23 is target.
[00:13:20] Ethan: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[00:13:25] [crosstalk and wrap-up for the next 10-28 minutes - brief scheduling, logistics, and clarifying questions. Sample snippets below are representative:]
[00:14:00] Priya: We'll anonymize data and send by Friday.
[00:14:05] Maya: Great - look out for the SOW and security pack.
[00:14:10] Liam: I'll drop the console link and the what-if screenshot in the follow-up.
[00:14:30] [00:20:00] End of call: thanks and bye.
---
Notes on transcript quality: some words like "KV cache" were transcribed as "k v cash" in a few spots; proper nouns sometimes inconsistent (Arbor vs Arbor Finance). Natural speech, interruptions, and an SE-led demo flow.
